accepted.question_text: Do there exist spherical orbifolds, meaning quotients of round spheres by finite isometry groups, that have exactly the same Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalues when multiplicities are ignored but have different Riemannian volumes?

evidence.quote: Question 1.1. Do there exist examples of eigenvalue equivalent spherical orbifolds whose volumes differ?
In Section 3 we will answer this question in the affirmative in every dimension n ≥ 9 by proving the following theorem.

accepted.question_text: For each dimension d, what is the greatest possible volume of a pair of spherical orbifolds of dimension d that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 1.4. What is the largest volume of an isospectral pair of d-dimensional non-isometric spherical orbifolds?

accepted.question_text: For each dimension d, what is the greatest possible volume of a pair of spherical space forms, that is, manifold quotients of the round sphere, that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 1.6. What is the largest volume of an isospectral and non-isometric pair of d-dimensional spherical space forms?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist two non-isometric towers of spherical manifolds, indexed by the same poset and related by finite-sheeted covering maps, such that at every level the two manifolds are isospectral?

evidence.quote: Question 1.12. Do there exist isospectral towers of spherical manifolds?
In Section 6 we will completely answer this question by constructing isospectral towers of lens spaces.

accepted.question_text: Which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces admit finite manifold quotients that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 1.15. Which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces cover isospectral and non-isometric manifolds?

accepted.question_text: Whenever a pair of spherical space forms of a fixed dimension has the largest possible volume among all isospectral non-isometric pairs in that dimension, must that extremal pair always be a pair of lens spaces?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7. Are isospectral and non-isometric spherical space forms of largest volume always lens spaces?

accepted.question_text: For odd-dimensional lens spaces of dimension 2n − 1 with fundamental group of order q, can there exist an isospectral non-isometric pair when n is congruent to −1 modulo φ(q)/2, where φ is Euler's totient function?

evidence.quote: Question 4.10. Are there isospectral and non-isometric (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces with fundamental group of order q satisfying n ≡ −1 (mod ϕ(q)/2)?

accepted.question_text: Do the compact Lie groups SU(3), Sp(2) (equivalently Spin(5)), Sp(3), or G2 contain pairs of finite subgroups that are almost conjugate but not conjugate?
accepted.context_brief: Almost conjugate subgroups in compact Lie groups

evidence.quote: Question 7.5. Are there almost conjugate and non-conjugate subgroups in SU(3) (resp. Sp(2) ≃ Spin(5), Sp(3) and G2)?

accepted.question_text: Which compact symmetric spaces of group type, without assuming simple connectivity, admit manifold quotients that are isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 7.6. Which compact symmetric spaces of group type (not necessarily simply connected) cover isospectral manifolds.

accepted.question_text: Study the analogue of the compact-symmetric-space quotient problem for orbifolds: which orbifolds covered by compact symmetric spaces admit isospectral non-isometric quotients?
accepted.context_brief: Orbifolds covered by compact symmetric spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 7.7. Study Question 1.15 in the context of orbifolds covered by compact symmetric spaces.

accepted.question_text: Fix a dimension d and a volume x. What is the largest possible cardinality of a family of spherical space forms of dimension d and volume x that are pairwise isospectral and pairwise non-isometric?
accepted.context_brief: Largest isospectral families at fixed dimension and volume

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1. Fix a dimension d. What is the maximal cardinality of an isospectral set of spherical space forms of volume x and dimension d?

accepted.question_text: Given a spherical orbifold of volume V, what general upper bound can one place on the size of an isospectral set of spherical orbifolds that contains it?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2. Let M be a spherical orbifold of volume V. What is an upper bound for the cardinality of an isospectral set of spherical orbifolds which contains M?

accepted.question_text: Is a generic lens space spectrally unique, meaning that within an appropriate family of lens spaces it has no non-isometric partner with the same Laplace spectrum?
accepted.context_brief: Generic spectral uniqueness of lens spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 8.5. Is a “generic” lens space spectrally unique?

accepted.question_text: For which dimensions 2n − 1 and orders q of the fundamental group is every lens space of volume vol(S^(2n−1))/q spectrally unique within the class of lens spaces with that same dimension and group order, so that no nontrivial isospectrality occurs?
accepted.context_brief: When lens spaces are spectrally unique

evidence.quote: Problem 8.7. Provide conditions on n and q such that L•(n, q) = L(n, q); that is, for which no (non-trivial) isospectrality is possible among (2n − 1)-dimensional lens spaces with volume vol(S2n−1)/q.

accepted.question_text: For spherical space forms, how much information does the Laplace spectrum determine about the length spectrum of closed geodesics, and conversely how closely are these two spectra related?

evidence.quote: Question 8.8. What is the relationship between the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum of a spherical space form?

accepted.question_text: If two spherical space forms have the same length spectrum of closed geodesics, must they be quotient commensurable, meaning that both arise as finite-index quotients inside a common finite group generated by their deck groups?

evidence.quote: Question 8.9. If two spherical space forms have the same length spectrum, must they be quotient commensurable?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist hyperbolic manifolds that are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions but are not strongly isospectral, meaning that some natural elliptic operators on associated bundles have different spectra?
accepted.context_brief: Hyperbolic manifolds: isospectral but not strongly isospectral

evidence.quote: Question 8.10. Are there isospectral hyperbolic manifolds that are not strongly isospectral?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist hyperbolic manifolds that are p-isospectral for every degree p, meaning the Hodge-Laplace operators on p-forms all have the same spectra, but are nevertheless not strongly isospectral?
accepted.context_brief: Hyperbolic manifolds: p-isospectral but not strongly isospectral

evidence.quote: Question 8.11. Are there hyperbolic manifolds p-isospectral for all p that are not strongly isospectral?

trace.notes: Mapped the paper from the title page and contents. The document is a survey with sections 1-7 and a dedicated Section 8 titled 'Open problems and questions'.
Scanned the introduction and extracted explicit Question 1.1, Question 1.4, Question 1.6, Question 1.12, and Question 1.15.
Scanned Section 4 and extracted Question 4.7 and Question 4.10 as unresolved follow-up questions about extremal-volume spherical space forms and congruence conditions for lens spaces.
Scanned Section 7 and extracted Question 7.5, Question 7.6, and Problem 7.7 on almost conjugate subgroups and compact symmetric spaces.
Scanned Section 8 and extracted Problems 8.1, 8.2, 8.5, 8.7 and Questions 8.8, 8.9, 8.10, 8.11 as the paper's main remaining open problems.
Expanded 'eigenvalue equivalent' into a self-contained description using the paper's introductory explanation and preserved the fact that multiplicities are ignored.
Rewrote the extremal-volume question so it explicitly asks for the maximal volume of an isospectral non-isometric orbifold pair in a fixed dimension.
Expanded 'spherical space forms' to clarify that the objects are manifold quotients of the round sphere.
Made the tower question self-contained by inlining that the indexing set is a poset and the structure maps are finite-sheeted coverings.
Rephrased the covering question to emphasize finite manifold quotients of compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces.
Clarified that the question asks whether extremal largest-volume pairs must always be lens spaces.
Expanded the modular condition by naming Euler's totient function and explaining the dimension/fundamental-group parameters.
Spelled out the list of compact Lie groups mentioned in the source and kept the almost-conjugate versus non-conjugate distinction explicit.
Rewrote the group-type symmetric-space question to make the non-simply-connected setting explicit.
Converted the imperative problem statement into a standalone research question about orbifolds covered by compact symmetric spaces.
Expanded 'isospectral set' into pairwise isospectral and pairwise non-isometric spherical space forms with fixed dimension and volume.
Rewrote the upper-bound problem into a self-contained question parameterized by a spherical orbifold M of volume V.
Added the intended meaning of spectral uniqueness in the lens-space setting so the question stands alone.
Inlined the meaning of L•(n, q) = L(n, q) by stating that no nontrivial isospectrality occurs among lens spaces with the given dimension and group order.
Expanded the short source question to name the length spectrum of closed geodesics and its relation to the Laplace spectrum.
Made quotient commensurability explicit by paraphrasing the paper's description using common finite quotients/deck groups.
Added the meaning of strong isospectrality so the hyperbolic-manifold question is understandable without nearby source text.
Expanded p-isospectrality to explain that the Hodge-Laplace operators on p-forms agree for every degree p.

Checked for near-duplicate open problems across the introduction and Section 8. Introductory questions answered later in the paper were kept distinct from unresolved Section 8 problems because they ask substantively different things.
All accepted items include page-numbered verbatim evidence, avoid dangling references to sections or theorem numbers, and only inline context that is supported by nearby source text.
